verses.text: “I’ve told you all this so you won’t stumble and fall away.
They’ll throw you out of the synagogues. The time is coming when anyone who kills you will think they’re serving God.
They’ll do this because they haven’t known the Father or me.
I’ve told you ahead of time, so when it happens, you’ll remember I warned you. I didn’t tell you from the beginning because I was with you.
But now I’m going to the One who sent me. None of you is asking me, ‘Where are you going?’
Because I’ve told you this, sadness has filled your heart.
Still, I’m telling you the truth: it’s better for you if I go. If I don’t go, the Advocate won’t come to you. But if I go, I’ll send him to you.
When he comes, he will confront the world about sin, righteousness, and judgment:
sin, because people don’t believe in me;
righteousness, because I’m going to my Father, and you won’t see me anymore;
and judgment, because the ruler of this world has already been judged.
“I still have a lot to tell you, but you can’t take it all in right now.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he’ll guide you into all truth. He won’t speak on his own; he’ll say what he hears and tell you what’s coming.
He’ll bring me glory, because he’ll take what belongs to me and make it known to you.
Everything the Father has is mine. That’s why I said the Spirit will take what is mine and make it known to you.
“In a little while, you won’t see me. Then, after another little while, you will see me.”

Some of his disciples said to one another, “What does he mean by, ‘In a little while you won’t see me, and then after another little while you will’? And what does he mean, ‘Because I’m going to the Father’?”
They kept asking, “What does he mean by ‘a little while’? We don’t know what he’s saying.”
Jesus knew they wanted to ask him, so he said, “Are you asking each other what I meant by, ‘In a little while you won’t see me, and then after another little while you will’?
I’m telling you the truth: you’ll cry and grieve, while the world celebrates. You’ll be hurting, but your pain will turn into joy.
When a woman is giving birth, she goes through pain because her time has come. But once the baby is born, she doesn’t dwell on the pain anymore; she’s glad a child has come into the world.
You’re hurting now, but I’ll see you again. Then your heart will rejoice, and nobody can take that joy away. 🌅
“When that day comes, you won’t ask me questions. I’m telling you the truth: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
Until now, you haven’t asked for anything in my name. Ask, and you’ll receive, so your joy can be complete.
“I’ve been speaking to you with figures of speech. The time is coming when I won’t use figures of speech anymore; I’ll tell you plainly about the Father.
When that day comes, you’ll ask in my name. I’m not saying that I’ll ask the Father for you,
because the Father himself loves you. You’ve loved me and believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father and entered the world. Now I’m leaving the world and going back to the Father.”
His disciples said, “Look, now you’re speaking plainly. You’re not using figures of speech.
Now we know you know everything, and nobody needs to question you. That’s why we believe you came from God.”
Jesus answered, “So now you believe?
Look, the time is coming—in fact, it’s already here—when you’ll scatter, each of you going your own way, and leave me alone. But I’m not alone; the Father is with me.
I’ve told you all this so you can have peace in me. In this world you’ll have trouble. But take heart—I’ve overcome the world.” 💪
